title.heading: Rev 1 rework
title.text:
One cut, one wire, one resistor, one zener.
4 steps on the module side of the board.

labels.title: rbmod carrier
labels.text: Under the display. The rework is done on the side the modules sit on.

chips.text: Wire GPIO 15 to the outer pad

labels.title: M1 · RP2350-CAN
labels.text: The IOmcu module, on pin headers.

labels.title: M7 · buck module
labels.text: Makes the 5 V of the programming ports.

labels.title: Eight 120 Ω footprints
labels.text: Not fitted. A track joins the two pads of each.

labels.title: PROGP03 runs to GPIO 26
labels.text: GPIO 26 is an ADC pin and not 5 V tolerant. A Hitec or KST servo pulls the programming line up to its supply.

labels.title: Scratch the track open at R1
labels.text: Between the two pads of R1, the end footprint of the row, next to J1 pin 1. Afterwards the two pads must not conduct to each other.

labels.title: Wire GPIO 15 to the outer pad
labels.text: From the module's pad 20, GP15, to the pad that leads on to J1. GPIO 26 ends at the inner pad and stays unused.

labels.title: 2.2 kΩ from EN to GND
labels.text: On top of the module, from EN to the GND pad beside it. An open EN reads as on: the pull-down keeps the ports' 5 V off while the IOmcu is in reset, in BOOTSEL or unpowered.

labels.title: 5.6 V zener from OUT+ to GND
labels.text: A 2 W or 5 W part, its banded end, the cathode, on OUT+. A braking servo feeds energy back into the 5 V, and M7 latches off above about 6.0 V. The zener takes that energy.

scenes.heading: Rev 1 rework
items: Scratch the track open between the pads of R1
Wire GP15, pad 20, to R1's outer pad
2.2 kΩ from M7's EN to GND
5.6 V zener from M7's OUT+ to GND, cathode on OUT+
scenes.note: The carrier firmware relies on steps 1 to 3. Reference: docs/Carrier.md, Rev 1 rework.
